title: Reddit's Q3 User Miss Led by Soft Search-Referral Traffic, BofA Says
detail:
PREMIUM
Reddit's Q3 User Miss Led by Soft Search-Referral Traffic, BofA Says
MT Newswires
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 10:59 AM EDT 1 min read
RDDT
BAC
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit's (RDDT) Q3 user miss was driven by weaker search-referral traffic, which declined further in October, with current trends pointing to a low-double-digit decline in daily active users in Q4, BofA Securities said Friday in a note.

Reddit's Q3 revenue was $895 million, exceeding Street estimates. Q3 daily active users were 130.3 million, below the Street consensus, driven by a decline in Google search referral traffic, according to the note.

The company is shifting marketing spend toward app installs and plans to test a logged-in-only experience internationally in Q4, BofA noted. The firm expects the transition to a logged-in user experience to take multiple quarters and weigh on headline traffic trends, the note added.

However, the change could result in a higher quality user base, improve monetization and eliminate the Google traffic overhang, the brokerage said. BofA expects sentiment to remain subdued for a few quarters until Reddit demonstrates positive growth momentum for US logged-in users.

BofA kept a neutral rating on Reddit and lowered its price target to $135 from $190.

Shares of Reddit were down 26% in Friday trading.

title: Apple faces margin pressure and uneven iPhone demand as launch schedule shifts, Bank of America says

Apple faces margin pressure and uneven iPhone demand as launch schedule shifts, Bank of America says

Trading disclosure
Apple faces margin pressure and uneven iPhone demand as launch schedule shifts, Bank of America says Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL, XETRA:APC) is expected to deliver a modest earnings beat for its September quarter, but a staggered iPhone launch, rising component costs and weaker services growth could weigh on its December results, according to Bank of America (BofA).

The brokerage expects September-quarter revenue of $113 billion and earnings per share of $1.97, compared with Wall Street estimates of $114 billion and $1.99, respectively, ahead of results due after the market closes on November 2.

The bank said the staggered launch of new iPhone models would affect quarterly sales patterns, with the Pro, Pro Max and Duo models released in September, while the base model and Air are scheduled for March.

The brokerage lowered its financial 2027 iPhone shipment forecast by 9 million units to 247 million, compared with the Street estimate of 260 million, reflecting a more cautious view of demand.

It expects component cost inflation, particularly for memory, to put pressure on gross margins over the coming quarters, although higher prices, product mix and cost-saving measures should offset part of the impact.

BofA estimates that memory costs could reduce iPhone gross margins by 900 basis points before pricing, mix and cost actions narrow the impact to 500 basis points, with the overall effect on company gross margin estimated at 250 basis points.

The brokerage forecasts total gross margin of 43.6% to 44.6% in the March quarter, below the 47.7% consensus estimate, and said the pressure should prove temporary, with margins recovering towards the end of financial 2027 and into financial 2028.

Services revenue is another concern, with BofA expecting growth of 10% in the September quarter, while App Store revenue growth slowed to 1.8% from 3.8% in the previous quarter.

The brokerage reiterated its 'buy' rating and $370 price target, but cautioned that near-term results could face headwinds relative to market expectations.

title: Starbucks recovery gains momentum as sales growth and margins improve, brokers say
detail:
Starbucks recovery gains momentum as sales growth and margins improve, brokers say
Proactive

SBUX
BAC
SRB
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Starbucks Corp (NASDAQ:SBUX, XETRA:SRB) is showing signs of a sustained business recovery, with stronger US sales, improving profitability and cost savings supporting its latest earnings beat, while Jefferies and Bank of America (BofA) see scope for further progress in financial 2027.

The coffee chain reported US same-store sales growth of 7.7% in the fourth quarter, ahead of the 7% analyst consensus, driven by a 2.4% increase in customer traffic and a 5.2% rise in average spending.

Adjusted earnings per share were $0.80, beating the 72-cent consensus estimate, while operating margin increased to 14%, against expectations of 12.7%, as lower store operating expenses and general and administrative costs supported profitability.

International same-store sales grew 0.9%, below the 3.3% consensus, as stronger performance in the UK was offset by weaker results in Japan.

Jefferies said product innovation, rewards, delivery and improvements to stores were contributing to the recovery, with more than 1,700 store upgrades completed by the end of financial 2026 and another 2,000 planned for financial 2027.

Starbucks forecast North American same-store sales growth of 4% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.15 to $3.25 for financial 2027, broadly in line with the $3.16 analyst consensus at the midpoint.

The company expects operating margin to reach 13.5% to 14%, compared with 11.9% in financial 2026, as cost savings and operational improvements support profitability.

BofA said management had set conservative targets for sales growth and earnings, leaving room for further upgrades as stronger same-store sales and cost reductions flow through to profits.

Jefferies took a more cautious view, forecasting North American same-store sales growth of 3.3% and an operating margin of 13.2% in financial 2027, below management's outlook.

The broker reiterated its 'hold' rating and $101 price target, arguing that investor optimism was already reflected in the valuation and questions remained over the sustainability of the recovery.

BofA raised its price target to $141 from $136, maintaining its positive outlook on the recovery, and said Starbucks could deliver further earnings upgrades as sales growth and cost savings exceed management's conservative forecasts.

title: Caterpillar's Strong Earnings Power Remains Intact, BofA Securities Says
detail:
PREMIUM
Caterpillar's Strong Earnings Power Remains Intact, BofA Securities Says
MT Newswires
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 10:46 AM EDT 1 min read
CAT
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Caterpillar's (CAT) strong earnings power remains intact, with potential to grow earnings per share amid the company's conservative guidance and macro uncertainty, BofA Securities said in a Friday note.

The company reported Q3 adjusted profit of $7.20 per share, up from $4.95 a year earlier, as sales and revenue rose to $20.68 billion from $17.64 billion. Caterpillar shares fell after the results and BofA attributed this to a narrow earnings beat.

BofA also noted that Caterpillar did not raise its outlook, even with a record $78 billion backlog, limiting EPS revisions.

Caterpillar's backlog and EPS outlook entail minimal capital requirements, yet the company trades at a free cash flow yield of 5%, the brokerage said. The company still has the potential to generate 15% of its market cap in free cash flow in the coming years, BofA added.

BofA has a buy rating on Caterpillar, with a lower price target of $746 from $850 previously.

Both Bank of America and Roth Capital downgraded Intel to 'Neutral' from 'Buy'.

Bank of America also lowered its estimate of the company's 2030 earnings power.

Citi called Intel's quarterly performance a 'strong beat' but said its December-quarter outlook was 'weak.'

Intel (INTC) shares were on track to wipe out a quarter of their market capitalization and see their worst day in over two years in pre-market trade on Friday after a slew of price target cuts and downgrades from Wall Street following the tech giant's third-quarter earnings.

Analysts broadly agree that Intel's near-term outlook is shaky, with weaker PC demand, manufacturing constraints, and delayed supply improvements weighing on expectations, according to TheFly.

INTC stock fell as much as 25% in pre-market trade, on track to see its biggest single-day dip since July 2024. If the stock falls more than 26%, it would mark its biggest dip since April 1979, when it fell over 33%.

INTC stock daily gains over the past years on October 30 as of 7:30 a.m. ET | Source: Koyfin

If the losses hold through the regular session, the stock would also hit a six-month low. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Intel remained in 'bullish' territory over the past day.

INTC stock retail sentiment on October 30 as of 7:30 a.m. ET | Source: Stocktwits
INTC Stock Gets Downgraded

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya downgraded Intel to 'Neutral' from 'Buy' and lowered the price target to $100 from $145. He said the company's turnaround had been pushed out by PC and supply headwinds, while a "surprisingly sharp drop" in PC shipments offset strength in data center demand.

Arya also pointed to a lack of progress in attracting outside foundry customers, saying Intel "has not communicated enough traction with external foundry customers." The firm lowered its estimate of Intel's 2030 earnings power to $5 to $6 per share from $6 to $7.

Roth Capital analyst Suji Desilva also downgraded Intel to 'Neutral' from 'Buy' and lowered his price target to $70 from $120. While "encouraged" by continued data center growth and the expansion of Intel's custom data center business, Desilva said manufacturing constraints could limit further upside.

Intel Had A 'Strong Beat' But 'Weak' Outlook

While Citi stated that Intel's third-quarter performance was a "strong beat," it also noted that the company's December-quarter outlook was "weak," citing the impact of a manufacturing accident that shut down Fab 28 in Israel and softer PC demand. The firm lowered its price target to $100 from $130 while maintaining a 'Buy' rating.

title: JPMorgan Raises NII Outlook: Is JPM Stock Too Expensive?
detail:
JPMorgan Raises NII Outlook: Is JPM Stock Too Expensive?
Swayta Shah

JPM
BAC
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

JPMorgan JPM has raised its net interest income (NII) outlook for 2026, supported by steady loan growth, higher deposit balances and resilient customer activity. The banking giant also provided an encouraging preliminary NII outlook for 2027, suggesting that spread income momentum could continue into next year.

In the third quarter of 2026, JPMorgan's NII increased 13% year over year to $27.1 billion. Its diversified business model, strong capital position and robust profitability further support its growth prospects. However, rising operating expenses, credit-related risks and a premium valuation remain concerns. Against this backdrop, should investors consider buying JPM shares?

JPMorgan's Upbeat NII Outlook Signals Further Growth

JPMorgan's NII prospects have strengthened considerably, reflecting favorable business trends and an improving interest-rate outlook. Following its third-quarter results, management raised its full-year 2026 total NII projection to approximately $106.2 billion from the previously expected $105.5 billion.

Similarly, NII excluding Markets is now anticipated to reach approximately $97.2 billion, up from the earlier projection of $96.5 billion. For the fourth quarter, management expects total NII of roughly $28 billion and NII excluding Markets of $25.5 billion.

JPMorgan provided a preliminary central-case outlook for 2027 NII excluding Markets of approximately $107 billion. This suggests growth of roughly 10% from the implied 2026 level, signaling management's confidence in continued business expansion.

The upbeat outlook is supported by sustained growth in lending and deposits, along with expectations of a favorable interest-rate environment. Higher loan balances and improved yields on interest-earning assets are expected to support interest income, while JPMorgan's extensive deposit franchise provides a competitive funding advantage. Nonetheless, management emphasized that its 2027 projections remain preliminary and depend on several economic and market assumptions.

JPM's Loan and Deposit Growth Supports NII Momentum

JPMorgan's robust balance sheet expansion reinforces its optimistic NII outlook. In the third quarter of 2026, average loans increased 10% year over year to $1.6 trillion, while average deposits grew 8% to $2.7 trillion.

NII excluding Markets advanced 6% year over year to $24.7 billion, driven by higher deposit balances, increased credit card balances and growth in wholesale lending. These factors more than offset the adverse impact of lower interest rates.

Continued lending demand across consumer and commercial businesses, coupled with deposit growth, is expected to support interest-earning asset expansion. Moreover, JPMorgan's diversified deposit base and established customer relationships provide a relatively stable funding source, strengthening its ability to sustain spread income.

The improving NII outlook is not limited to JPMorgan. Bank of America BAC expects full-year 2026 NII on a fully taxable-equivalent (FTE) basis to grow approximately 8% year over year, with growth of 8% or more anticipated for 2027. Likewise, Citigroup C now expects NII excluding Markets to grow in the mid-to-high 6% range in 2026, an improvement from its previous forecast of growth at the high end of the 5-6% range.

These encouraging projections indicate broader NII growth opportunities across major U.S. banks, supported by loan and deposit expansion and asset repricing. However, changes in interest rates, deposit pricing and economic conditions could influence the extent of future gains.

title: Bank of America vs. Goldman Sachs: Two Wall Street Giants, Two Very Different Revenue Stories
detail:
Bank of America vs. Goldman Sachs: Two Wall Street Giants, Two Very Different Revenue Stories
RJ Fulton, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:25 AM EDT 5 min read
BAC
GS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) are two of Wall Street's biggest names, but their revenue trends reveal an interesting contrast.

While both benefit from lending, trading, and overall investment activity, their businesses respond differently to current market conditions. With inflation remaining stubborn and capital markets active, the question for investors is which business is better positioned for sustained growth.

Bank of America: Steady Quarterly Revenue Trends

Bank of America generates revenue through consumer banking, lending, wealth management, and investment banking services, serving individuals, businesses, and institutions worldwide.

The company's latest earnings highlight the strength of its diversified business model. In the third quarter of 2026, net interest income increased 8% year over year to $16.4 billion, supported by higher loan and deposit balances. Meanwhile, its wealth management division reported 13% revenue growth, benefiting from rising asset management fees and growing client assets. Together, these businesses provide multiple sources of income, helping Bank of America maintain relatively consistent revenue even as financial market conditions change.

Goldman Sachs: Recent Quarterly Revenue Volatility

Goldman Sachs earns revenue through investment banking, securities trading, asset management, and wealth management services, serving corporations, institutional investors, and individuals worldwide.

The company's latest earnings highlight its sensitivity to financial market activity and corporate dealmaking. In the third quarter of 2026, Goldman Sachs reported $18.7 billion in net revenue, supported by strong trading activity and demand for investment banking services. During the first nine months of 2026, investment banking fees increased 40% year over year, while equities revenue jumped 57%. These results demonstrate how Goldman Sachs can benefit from increased market activity, but also why its revenue can fluctuate more significantly than that of traditional banks when trading conditions and dealmaking slow.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue here refers to the data provider's standardized income-statement revenue line item, which for banks in this dataset is defined as interest income plus non-interest income and is not net of interest expense, providing investors a fundamental top-line measure to evaluate how much money a business effectively generates.

title: Alphabet just had its worst day as a public company. BofA now values Google search at a lower multiple than fossil fuel stocks
detail:
Alphabet just had its worst day as a public company. BofA now values Google search at a lower multiple than fossil fuel stocks
Nick Lichtenberg
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:10 PM EDT 4 min read
GOOG
BAC
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Google search, the business that paid for two decades of Alphabet's ambitions, is now valued at about 10 times earnings, by Bank of America's count. The S&P 500 trades at 18.7x forward earnings, according to FactSet. Energy, the market's cheapest sector, trades at 13x.

That math pummeled the stock Thursday. Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% to $283.82, their worst day since they began trading in 2004. The decline wiped out about $482 billion in market value. Previously, Alphabet's worst day was in March 2020 when the stock dropped 11.6%.

The trigger was the search business—the same juggernaut that turned Google into a verb. Search and other revenue grew 12% in the third quarter to $63.35 billion. Analysts expected 15%. That miss on growth momentum compares to 17% growth in the second quarter and 19% in the first. Meanwhile, Google Cloud's revenue more than doubled, up 103% to $30.71 billion. But Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditures in the quarter, more than double a year earlier, and free cash flow came in at negative $9.1 billion, according to its earnings release.

Three months ago, BofA analyst Justin Post had the whole company at about 22x his 2027 earnings estimate, which he called in line with historical averages. On Thursday, at the after-hours price of about $291, he had it at about 19x, with core search at about 10x inside that. He kept his Buy rating, cut his price target to $380 from $430, and lowered the multiple he's willing to pay to 24 times from 27, citing the "slowdown in high-margin search growth."

"Search AI transition will fuel the bears," Post and co-author Nitin Bansal wrote.

"The bears will argue this is the first quarter that AI is starting to seriously hurt their search business," Pivotal Research CEO Jeffrey Wlodarczak said, as previously reported by Yahoo Finance.

More searches, slower growth

The search slowdown comes even as Google says more people are searching. "Our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it's been in the last 5 years," CEO Sundar Pichai said on Wednesday's earnings call.

BofA estimates search growth, excluding currency moves, slowed three percentage points from the prior quarter, "despite accelerating y/y query growth." The analysts put most of that on a comparison that was two points tougher than last quarter's. They wrote that Google indicated the shift of traffic to AI Overviews, the AI-written summaries at the top of results, was a small headwind in the quarter. They added that it's "likely bigger" internationally, where advertising loads in those summaries are just starting to ramp.
